title: Service General Setting area: startup modes and service security descriptors

provenance.note: Shape derived from Microsoft secedit/security-template documentation and well-known GptTmpl.inf layout. No native capture of this area exists in the repo yet; the first secedit /export capture on the disposable host must confirm or correct every entry here before any claim.

anchors.note: Certified WP-3 tranche evidence; proves the harness mechanics this scenario reuses, not this area.

operator_meaning: WinRM: automatic startup with an explicit DACL granting administrators full control
Spooler: disabled with an explicitly empty security descriptor field
W32Time: manual startup with no security descriptor field at all

derivations: Startup mode codes follow the secedit convention 2=automatic, 3=manual, 4=disabled; the certified tranche proves only that secedit accepts and round-trips authored sections, not these codes.

The service name is a quoted CSV field; the optional third field carries the service DACL as an SDDL string. The empty-string form (Spooler) and the absent-field form (W32Time) are distinct authored states and must not be conflated by the parser.

Studio's security_template.py currently has no typed accessor for this area: entries parse as opaque key/value lines under a known section name. Remediation must decide the typed model; this scenario fixes the wire truth it must honor.

open_questions: Does secedit /export normalize the SDDL (ordering, shorthand) or return it byte-identical? The comparison rule must be fixed from the first capture.
Does secedit /validate accept an entry whose startup code is present but the SDDL field is omitted entirely (W32Time row), or does it require the empty string form?
Which startup codes, if any, does secedit reject (0, 1, 5+)? Negative cases belong in the WP-8 failure-injection set.
